questions.title: The Yeasts
questions.subtitle: Here we use 3 types of yeast
answers: Dry active yeast is the yeast found in stores as so-called classic baker's yeast and not fast-acting.
Instant dry yeast is freeze-dried yeast in the form of fine flakes. It does not need to be hydrated before use and allows for rapid rising.
Fresh yeast is the yeast found in stores as so-called fresh baker's yeast in the form of a cube paste.

questions.title: 💦 Hydration
questions.subtitle: Ratio between the total amount of water and the total amount of flour
answers: Ex 1: For a total of 100 g of water, I will have a total of 151.5 g of flour, which gives a dough hydration of 66%. Calculation: 100 ÷ 151.5 = 0.66 or 66%.
Ex 2: If I want to know the amount of water to add when I have 151.5 g of flour and I want a hydration of 66%, the calculation will be: 0.66 x 151.5 = 100 g of water in total to add.

tips.title: 💡 Tip:
tips.description: The more hydrated the dough, the more difficult it will be to handle, it will be more liquid and therefore more sticky. Recommended hydration: Between 62 & 75%

questions.title: 🍚 Poolish Ratio
questions.subtitle: Ratio between the amount of poolish and the total amount of dough
answers: We commonly use between 30 and 60% of poolish in the final amount of dough.

Ex: If I want 30% of poolish in my dough and 1 kg of final dough, the calculation will be: 1000 x 0.3 = 300 g. The poolish will therefore be 300 g and will be composed of 150 g of flour and 150 g of water.

tips.title: 💡 Tip:
tips.description: In general, a higher ratio of poolish is used in winter than in summer because fermentation is partly influenced by temperature. So putting more poolish in winter than in summer can help the final development of the dough.
